# measured-at: 0ea71c6 (fix/card-text-color) + uncommitted colour fix
# change:      src/ggrender/scene_card.go only, 4 insertions / 1 deletion:
#              1. RenderCard: explicit dc.SetColor(cardDark) before the 入职日
#                 label, which previously inherited cardBlue and painted
#                 #0098dc glyphs on a #0098dc chip (245 glyph px lost).
#              2. cardDark #111111 -> #000000. Both use sites (date chip,
#                 助理 label) sit on template elements that declare no
#                 color, so the browser default black is ground truth;
#                 assets/css/common.css has zero color declarations
#                 (grep -c color -> 0, exit=1) and template/Card.tmpl
#                 #regTime / #regTime div / 助理 div declare none either.
#              No coordinates, no font, no gate logic, no pixel_test.go.
# verified:    15 of 16 scenes are byte-identical before/after, proven by
#              `diff` of two `go test -run TestGGPixelParity -v` captures in
#              this worktree. ONLY the card line differs.
#              CAVEAT ON DIRECTION: card moved 0.96020 -> 0.96015 (-0.00005),
#              i.e. DOWN, not up. Per-region pixel counts show the colour fix
#              is correct (入职日 dark px 0 -> 258 vs baseline 245) but the
#              gg glyphs land ~3px higher and thicker than the Playwright
#              baseline, so the restored ink adds more mismatch than the
#              missing ink cost. See the report; this is a font-fidelity
#              follow-up, not a colour reversal.
